title: Peacemaking
definition: Peacemaking is the active pursuit of peace through truth, humility, righteousness, forgiveness, and love.
summary: Peacemaking reflects God's heart by seeking peace without compromising truth.
christFocus: Jesus is the Prince of Peace who reconciles sinners to God and calls His people to live as peacemakers.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Peacemaking is not avoiding conflict at any cost. Biblical peace is rooted in truth, righteousness, humility, and love. It does not ignore sin or sacrifice holiness for the appearance of harmony.

Peacemakers seek to reduce unnecessary conflict, speak truth with gentleness, pursue forgiveness, repair harm, and promote unity where possible.

Christ is the foundation of peace. Through Him, sinners are reconciled to God and empowered to pursue peace with others.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Some people confuse peace with silence, avoidance, or control. Peacemaking matters because God's people are called to actively pursue peace in ways that honor truth and love.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: When conflict arises, slow down, pray, listen carefully, speak truth gently, and seek what honors Christ. Refuse gossip, revenge, and unnecessary escalation.
